name: Plunnecke-Ruzsa, Dias da Silva-Hamidoune k-subset sums, Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa submultiplicativity
description: Classical sumset tools: Plunnecke-Ruzsa gives |sX - tX| <= C^{s+t}|X| for doubling C; Dias da Silva-Hamidoune (Erdos-Heilbronn type) gives the number of distinct sums of k distinct elements |Sigma_k(S)| >= k(m-k)+1 for a set of m integers (as stated in the task); Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa prove a Plunnecke-type inequality for different summands and a submultiplicativity |S| <= prod |S_i|^{1/(n-1)}. These give lower bounds on the number of distinct sums but only polynomial ones for fixed k.
authors_year_venue: Plunnecke 1970 / Ruzsa (classical); Dias da Silva-Hamidoune 1994 (Bull. London Math. Soc.) [uncertain]; Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa, 'Plunnecke's inequality for different summands', arXiv:0810.1488 (2008, Building Bridges). Plunnecke-Ruzsa as stated in arXiv:2407.18228 Lemma A.1.
status_and_verification: Classical peer-reviewed results. Verified against primary text only for Plunnecke-Ruzsa as quoted in arXiv:2407.18228 App. A (Lemma A.1) and Petridis' improvement |hA| = O(C^{h-1}|A|^{2-1/h}) as quoted there. Dias da Silva-Hamidoune bound taken from the task statement and memory; a web search returned only the GMR page (abstract-level snippet: different-summand Plunnecke and submultiplicativity |S| <= (prod |S_i|)^{1/(n-1)}), not the primary papers. Not read: GMR proofs; DdS-H proof. [uncertain]
key_theorem_or_bound: Plunnecke-Ruzsa (Lemma A.1 of 2407.18228): if |X+X| <= C|X| in an abelian group then |sX - tX| <= C^{s+t}|X|. Petridis: |hA| = O(C^{h-1}|A|^{2-1/h}) [as quoted in 2407.18228 Remark 7.1]. Dias da Silva-Hamidoune (task statement): |Sigma_k(S)| >= k(m-k)+1 for k-subset sums of an m-set of integers [uncertain: exact hypotheses not verified]. GMR: submultiplicativity |S| <= (prod_{i=1}^n |S_i|)^{1/(n-1)} (snippet) [uncertain: exact statement]. [uncertain]
regime_exponents: Fixed k gives polynomial bounds k(m-k)+1 about k m, trivially far below 2^{0.311n}. For k=cn, k(m-k)+1 is O(n^2), polynomial, so the DdS-H bound alone says nothing near 2^{0.311n}. Plunnecke at k=cn gives C^{cn}, exponential in n only for fixed C>1. Upper trivial bound is C(m,k) <= 2^{h(c)m}; no threshold at 0.5n/0.661n.
proof_type_and_tools: Combinatorial/algebraic: Plunnecke via graph/magnification ratio (Petridis proof); DdS-H via exterior algebra/polynomial method (Alon-Nathanson-Ruzsa style) [uncertain]; GMR via a Plunnecke-type inequality for different summands.
quantitative_loss: Plunnecke: exponential in s+t (C^{s+t}), so for k=Theta(n) subset-size sumsets an upper bound C^{Theta(n)} is not useful as an upper bound on size when only C is known, but a lower bound via inversion (|kA| >= |A|... ) is weak. DdS-H is linear in k(m-k) (polynomial), far from the exponential bounds required; it does not survive exponential energy.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Worst case over all sets (deterministic inequalities). Lower bounds are tight for arithmetic progressions, so they cannot improve for structured instances.
coefficient_set: Plain subsets (distinct elements, {0,1}) for Sigma_k; Plunnecke uses sums/differences with repetition (multiset sumsets sX); GMR for general abelian group sumsets A+B_{i}.
subset_size_regime: DdS-H: k-subsets with fixed k typically (bound k(m-k)+1 holds for 1<=k<=m but is tight for APs, polynomial); Plunnecke: iterated sumsets with s fixed constant. Needs extension to k=Theta(n).
relevance_to_Nc: By Cauchy-Schwarz, the number of equal-sum pairs of k-subsets is at least C(m,k)^2/|Sigma_k(S)|, so any upper bound on the number of distinct k-subset sums |Sigma_k| gives a lower bound on N_c-type collision counts; Plunnecke-Ruzsa links |Sigma_k| growth to the doubling of the half-sums. The Dias da Silva-Hamidoune bound is a LOWER bound on |Sigma_k|, so it yields only a trivial upper bound on collisions (about C(m,k)^2/(k(m-k)+1) is not a constraint). Net: little direct use for N_c. [uncertain]
relevance_to_Dstar: Lower bounds on D* (distinct sums of subsets of size k) are exactly what DdS-H provides: D* >= k(m-k)+1 with m=n/2, k=cn gives only polynomial D*. To forbid D* <= 2^{0.311n} for hard instances, one would need a bound like |Sigma_k(S)| >= 2^{0.311n} unless S has structure (small doubling); Plunnecke-Ruzsa gives the converse (if D* small then doubling small so structure). No theorem reaching 2^{0.311n} is claimed. [uncertain]
applicability_gap: (1) DdS-H is a polynomial lower bound sharp for APs; hard instances have exponentially many sums, so no help. (2) Plunnecke needs small doubling C=O(1), losing C^{k}. (3) k=Theta(n) vs fixed k: constants k(m-k) are not exponent-tight. (4) Distinct-element (Erdos-Heilbronn) vs multiset sums distinction. (5) GMR requires the information on all A+B_{i1}+... sumsets.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Arithmetic progressions attain |Sigma_k| = k(m-k)+1 (extremal for DdS-H), so structure collapses D*; Sidon sets have |Sigma_k| = C(m,k) (maximal); rank-d GAP with random generators interpolate with |Sigma_k| about (k(m-k))^{d}-ish polynomial. These probe D* limits [uncertain].
dependency_chain: Plunnecke-Ruzsa -> Freiman (2407.18228) -> constructive structure; DdS-H -> lower bound on D* in the AP extreme; GMR submultiplicativity -> combine different summand half-sums; links to BSG (energy->doubling) and to AKKN (bins vs number of sums).
constructiveness: Plunnecke-Ruzsa is non-constructive but provides a polynomial-time verifiable sumset bound; DdS-H is a pure inequality (no algorithm needed). Constructive Plunnecke needs only computation of sumsets. Costs are those of enumerating sumsets (exponential for k=Theta(n)).
lean_formalizable: Plunnecke-Ruzsa has a formalized Isabelle AFP entry (Pluennecke_Ruzsa_Inequality, per search results); Lean mathlib-free formalization is plausible for the finite-set case (Petridis proof is short). DdS-H via polynomial method is harder.
computational_check: Source papers are theory (no experiments). Repo can brute-force |Sigma_k(S)| for n<=40 half-sets (m=20, k=10: C(20,10)=184756 subsets) and compare with k(m-k)+1=101 and with C(m,k); also measure doubling of half-sums vs Plunnecke prediction.
next_experiment: Compute |Sigma_k(S)| for k=m/2 for random, AP, Sidon and rank-d GAP sets (m<=24) and fit log2|Sigma_k|/m against doubling constant of S, to see whether Plunnecke-Ruzsa (C^k) is predictive at k=Theta(m).
open_issues: Exact DdS-H statement/hypotheses (integers vs Z_p, distinct elements) unverified here; Plunnecke-Ruzsa constants/exponents in k=Theta(n) regime; no known generalization giving exponential D* lower bounds for non-structured S.
